- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or mildly bearish; model reacts too slowly to downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp spikes, then undercorrects in subsequent periods.
- Forecast lags in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon; true price often moves faster than model anticipates.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to smooth out extremes, leading to underprediction of volatility-driven price swings.
- In periods of strong upward sentiment, model often fails to capture the full magnitude of the rally, especially in the first 10 days.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-period, model delays correction, leading to persistent overestimation of price until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates price peaks in the final 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is bullish but fading.
